request_debug.prompt_preview:
You write per-candidate post-mortems for a slopmortem pipeline. Given a fresh pitch and one dead-startup canonical document, produce a single LLMSynthesis JSON object that explains why this dead startup is similar, where the new pitch could diverge, what killed the dead startup, and what the new founder should learn.

Rules:
- Ground every claim in the candidate document or in tool calls. Do not invent facts.
- A `Trusted facts` block (typed pipeline data — not user input) appears below the pitc

response.text: {"candidate_id":"rethinkdb::devtools","name":"rethinkdb","one_liner":"Free and open-source distributed document database that failed to build a sustainable commercial business around its real-time change-feed technology.","similarity":{"business_model":{"score":1,"rationale":"RethinkDB was a free open-source product with no recurring per-seat or usage-based subscription; the new pitch is a per-driver B2B SaaS with usage overages — fundamentally different monetization structures."},"market":{"score":1,"rationale":"RethinkDB targeted developers building real-time applications globally; the new pitch targets US regional 3PL operators in logistics — entirely different verticals, buyers, and geographies."},"gtm":{"score":1,"rationale":"RethinkDB relied on open-source community adoption and developer word-of-mouth; the new pitch implies direct B2B sales to logistics operators, a completely different go-to-market motion."},"stage_scale":{"score":3,"rationale":"Both were early-stage, VC-backed (RethinkDB via Y Combinator) companies that struggled to cross from product traction to sustainable revenue before running out of runway — a broadly shared stage challenge."}},"why_similar":"The only meaningful similarity is at the stage/scale level: both companies are early-stage, venture-backed startups that face the core challenge of converting product usage into sustainable recurring revenue before capital runs dry. RethinkDB's story is a cautionary tale about building a technically impressive product without a viable monetization path, a risk any early-stage SaaS startup shares in principle.","where_diverged":"Nearly every concrete dimension diverges. (1) Business model: RethinkDB was free/open-source with no subscription; the new pitch is a paid per-driver SaaS with usage overages. (2) Market/sector: RethinkDB was a distributed database for developers (devtools, global); the new pitch is a logistics SaaS for US regional 3PLs (logistics_supply_chain, US). (3) Customer type: developers vs. logistics operations managers/dispatchers. (4) Product type: open-source infrastructure software vs. a vertical SaaS with a route-optimizer and dispatcher cockpit UI. (5) Geography: global developer audience vs. US-focused regional logistics operators.","failure_causes":["inability to monetize an open-source product","no sustainable commercial model around free software","failure to convert developer adoption into paying enterprise customers","open-source licensing undermined pricing power","loss of engineering team to acqui-hire (Stripe) signaling capital exhaustion","market timing mismatch — real-time database demand did not scale fast enough to support the business"],"lessons_for_input":["Never build your core product on a free/open-source model unless you have a clearly validated paid tier from day one — ensure your per-driver subscription pricing is tested before launch.","Define a payback period for CAC against your per-driver subscription ARPU early; RethinkDB collapsed partly because usage never converted to revenue.","Anchor the product to a specific, measurable operational pain (e.g., dispatcher hours saved, fuel cost reduction) so logistics buyers can justify budget — pure technical elegance does not sell in operations-heavy verticals.","Secure multi-year contracts with anchor 3PL customers before scaling headcount; RethinkDB ran out of runway without a committed revenue base.","Plan for usage-overage abuse or under-consumption: model both scenarios and set contractual minimums so revenue does not collapse if drivers go underutilized."]}
